AfterAddedToRoom.maps_to: PunchConstruct.__init__ (punch_construct.py:29-40) for the Artifact; _PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters (events/punch_off.py:22-30) for the HP reduction
AfterAddedToRoom.issue: PunchConstruct.StartingHpReduction is ported onto the wrong HP field: the game reduces CURRENT hp and leaves MAX hp at 55, the sim reduces MAX hp. PunchConstruct.cs:75-78 (inside AfterAddedToRoom) is `if (StartingHpReduction > 0) Creature.SetCurrentHpInternal(Math.Max(1, Creature.CurrentHp - StartingHpReduction))` - MaxInitialHp is a flat 55 (:33-35, non-ascension) and nothing touches MaxHp. The sim has no StartingHpReduction member at all; the Punch-Off encounter open-codes it as `m.max_hp = max(1, m.max_hp - reduction); m.hp = min(m.hp, m.max_hp)` (events/punch_off.py:27-28). So a Punch-Off construct that the game shows at '46/55' the sim shows at '46/46'. Observables: (a) the HP bar and the recorded EnemyState both carry max_hp, and the conformance replay compares the (name, hp, max_hp) triple positionally (combat_driver.py:184-191), so every Punch-Off fight reports an 'enemies' Divergence on max_hp; (b) any effect reading or restoring max HP - a heal, a percentage-of-max computation, the parity Niche uniqueness roll - sees 46 instead of 55; (c) the reduction is clamped against the wrong bound, so `max(1, ...)` protects max_hp where the game protects current hp.
AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: The hook has two clauses and they get different answers. CLAUSE 1, ArtifactPower 1 (PunchConstruct.cs:74 -> punch_construct.py:40): deliberate-divergence by SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, whose three clauses all hold - the amount is the literal 1, the power is self-applied with no card, and the initial state is a MoveState (READY_MOVE, or FAST_PUNCH_MOVE under StartsWithFastPunch), so monster_state_machine step 30's sticky no-op means the first roll reads nothing. RULE 7 NOTE: that shared rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does not hash. CLAUSE 2, StartingHpReduction: the gap above. EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py punchoff-hp` on a real Punch-Off CombatState (seed 4): 'sim punch-off construct 0: hp=53 max_hp=53 initial_move=FAST_PUNCH_MOVE' and 'sim punch-off construct 1: hp=49 max_hp=49 initial_move=READY_MOVE', against a game MaxHp of 55 for both. LIVE under rule 6, both sides reachable on ported content: the same probe prints 'punch_off in the sim's Underdocks event pool: True | registered class: <class sts2_rl.events.punch_off.PunchOff>' (events/__init__.py:73-76 lists it in UNDERDOCKS_EVENTS), the encounter is PunchOffEventEncounter's port and the reduction fires unconditionally for BOTH constructs - PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17,19 roll Rng.NextInt(2, 10), i.e. 2..9, never 0, and events/punch_off.py:26 rolls the matching randint(2, 9), so `StartingHpReduction > 0` is always true. The gap needs no relic, no potion and no player choice beyond taking the fight. Note the range and the first-construct StartsWithFastPunch flag are both ported CORRECTLY - only the field the reduction lands on is wrong.

guards.what: creature_card_cmds step 26 - and why this is a DIFFERENT method
guards.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 7 asks whether this unit makes the dormant SetMaxAndCurrentHp finding live. It does not: PunchConstruct.cs:77 calls SetCurrentHpInternal, which is the game's own raw current-HP setter for exactly this purpose, so a sim assignment that skips the hooks is faithful to the source here. The divergence recorded on AfterAddedToRoom is about WHICH FIELD is written, not about the hooks the write skips.

Class 10: StartsWithFastPunch and StartingHpReduction are both set at generation time and never reset, and the sim rebuilds the monster per combat, so nothing latches. Class 18 (TestMode.IsOn arms): no fork in this model.
